label: Elliptic Coordinates
notes: Appendix 20 introduces confocal conics as a curvilinear coordinate system. Open by stressing the payoff: certain hard mechanical problems become solvable because the Hamilton-Jacobi equation separates in these coordinates. Name the three classical examples we will reach, the geodesics on an ellipsoid, two fixed centres, and elliptic billiards.

label: Confocal Conics
notes: Fix two foci and let a single real parameter slide through the focal interval. Above the larger axis value we get nested ellipses; between the two roots we get hyperbolas. Emphasise that one algebraic family, indexed by lambda, produces both kinds of curve depending on which interval lambda lives in.

label: The Confocal Pencil
notes: Walk through the quadratic in lambda. For a generic plane point exactly two roots solve the confocal equation, one ellipse and one hyperbola. These two roots are the elliptic coordinates of the point. Stress that the construction is purely algebraic and extends verbatim to three dimensions.

label: Orthogonality
notes: The central structural fact: through each point one ellipse and one hyperbola pass, and they meet at a right angle. Sketch why, gradients of the two confocal functions are orthogonal. This orthogonality is what diagonalises the metric and makes separation of variables possible, so dwell on it.

label: The Coordinate Grid
notes: Show the full picture, nested ellipses crossing nested hyperbolas like lines of latitude and longitude, but warped to share two foci. Point out the foci as degenerate ellipses and the focal segment and its exterior axis as degenerate hyperbolas. This grid is the elliptic coordinate chart on the plane.

label: Separation in Hamilton-Jacobi
notes: Recall Hamilton-Jacobi from the main text: a complete integral of the partial differential equation gives the full solution by quadratures. In elliptic coordinates the kinetic energy and many natural potentials split into a sum where each variable appears alone, so the equation separates additively. That is the engine of integrability here.

label: Liouville Systems
notes: Frame the abstract template, a Liouville metric and potential of the additive confocal form. For such systems the Hamilton-Jacobi separates and one obtains a second integral beyond energy. Explain that elliptic coordinates are the canonical example, and that the separation constant is the new conserved quantity making the system integrable.

label: Geodesics on the Ellipsoid
notes: State Jacobi's theorem: geodesics on a triaxial ellipsoid are integrable, found by separating in confocal ellipsoidal coordinates. This was a landmark, the first nontrivial integrable geodesic flow. Mention the conserved Joachimsthal quantity and that geodesics oscillate between two confocal lines of curvature, foreshadowing the caustic picture.

label: Two Fixed Centres
notes: Describe the planar Euler problem, one mass moving under two fixed Newtonian attractors. In elliptic coordinates with foci at the centres the Hamilton-Jacobi separates, giving a second integral and integrability by quadratures. Note its role as a model for restricted gravitational motion and an early test bed for perturbation theory.

label: Elliptic Billiards
notes: Move to the billiard inside an ellipse. Every trajectory segment stays tangent to one fixed confocal conic, its caustic, an ellipse or a hyperbola. The caustic parameter is conserved at each bounce, so the billiard is integrable. This is the discrete shadow of the ellipsoid geodesic flow and a clean demonstration of the confocal invariant.

label: The Conserved Caustic
notes: Make the invariant explicit. Reflection in the ellipse preserves the confocal parameter of the line, so successive chords share one caustic. Connect this to the conserved separation constant, the product of distances or the confocal angle, that we met in the continuous problems. The same hidden symmetry runs through all three examples.

label: Synthesis
notes: Close by tying the thread together: confocal conics build an orthogonal chart, orthogonality separates Hamilton-Jacobi, separation yields a second integral, and that integral is integrability. The ellipsoid geodesics, two fixed centres, and elliptic billiards are three faces of one geometric idea. Invite students to run the notebook grid and trace a caustic.
